must_remember: The Maxwell velocity distribution assumes molecules are in continuous random motion, colliding elastically, with an isotropic distribution and statistically independent orthogonal velocity components.
The hierarchy of characteristic speeds is always $v_{mp} : v_{av} : v_{rms} = \sqrt{2} : \sqrt{\frac{8}{\pi}} : \sqrt{3} \approx 1.414 : 1.596 : 1.732$.
Root-mean-square speed is directly proportional to the square root of absolute temperature $T$ and inversely proportional to the square root of molecular mass $m$ or molar mass $M$.
The Maxwell speed distribution function starts at zero for $v = 0$, reaches a peak at $v_{mp}$, and decreases asymptotically as $v \to \infty$.
Average kinetic energy per molecule depends only on absolute temperature and is given by $\langle E \rangle = \frac{3}{2} k_B T$.

glossary.meaning: The speed possessed by the maximum fraction of gas molecules at a given temperature, given by $\sqrt{\frac{2k_B T}{m}}$.
The arithmetic average of the speeds of all gas molecules in thermal equilibrium, given by $\sqrt{\frac{8k_B T}{\pi m}}$.
The square root of the average of the squared speeds of the molecules, given by $\sqrt{\frac{3k_B T}{m}}$.
The relative probability of a state with energy $E$, proportional to $e^{-\frac{E}{k_B T}}$.
A spatial distribution where no single direction is preferred over any other.
